Shipment Status Events: Event-Driven Architecture & EDI 214

12 min read Updated: November 2026 By Rajvardhan Singh Rathore
In transportation networks, state changes arrive as asynchronous events. This guide unpacks event-sourcing architectures for freight, mapping legacy ANSI X12 EDI 214 transmissions to modern JSON Kafka event streams.

Event-Sourcing in Logistics Systems

Logistics tracking is naturally event-sourced. Rather than updating a single mutable row in place, platforms record every milestone scan as an append-only, immutable event. The current status of a shipment is simply the cumulative projection of all historical events ordered by timestamp.

Anatomy of an ANSI X12 EDI 214 Transaction

The standard EDI 214 (Transportation Carrier Shipment Status Message) uses standardized segments:

  • B10: Carrier Reference Number, Shipment ID, SCAC.
  • LX: Transaction set line number.
  • AT7: Shipment Status Details (Status Code, Status Reason, Date, Time, Time Code).
  • MS1: Equipment, Location (City, State, Postal Code, Country).
Raw EDI 214 Segment 
ST*214*0001~
B10*1029384*SHP-9921*FDXG~
LX*1~
AT7*X6*NS***20261111*1430*LT~
MS1*MEMPHIS*TN*USA~
SE*6*0001~

Kafka Avro / JSON Event Schema Specification

When translated into event streaming platforms, milestones adhere to strict JSON schemas:

JSON Event Schema 
{
  "event_id": "evt_01928374-1234-7000-8000-abcdef123456",
  "shipment_id": "shp_01928374-9999-7000-8000-111122223333",
  "source_protocol": "EDI_214",
  "carrier_scac": "FDXG",
  "canonical_status": "OUT_FOR_DELIVERY",
  "raw_status_code": "X6",
  "raw_reason_code": "NS",
  "event_timestamp": "2026-11-11T14:30:00Z",
  "location": {
    "city": "Memphis",
    "state": "TN",
    "country": "USA"
  }
}

Materializing Real-Time Status Projections

Kafka consumers aggregate incoming events, updating the master read-optimized view in PostgreSQL or Redis using idempotent transactions. Explore validation techniques in our SQL Validation Techniques Guide.
